chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Alternating sets, Leonard Feather, and the Lee and Lester band personnel
summary: He tells how the band alternated with others, who was in the band, and how Jimmy Rowles was replaced by Clyde Hart and then Sir Charles Thompson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, did your group alternate with these others...
You didn't have to be the rhythm section for everybody.

Oh, no, we alternated with everybody. But the hours... We played three or four sets a night. But just standing around in between was, you know, pretty terrible. And I found out later that Leonard Feather lived upstairs over it at Number 2 Sheridan Square; he lived right over the place. That's I guess when he had... He was relatively new here then, too.

So we worked out the contract, and rather than come back to Los Angeles I formed a trio with Sir Charles Thompson on piano and Louis Gonsales. I hadn't mentioned him, but he was a guitarist in Lee and Lester's band. I hadn't mentioned who was in the band either. It was Paul Campbell, trumpet; Bumps Myers, Hubert Myers, tenor and Lester, tenor; and Jimmy Rowles was playing piano. But Benny Goodman stole Jimmy Rowles from us, so when we went in to New York, Clyde Hart came into the band and did the whole engagement until just when we were almost ready to leave,
and then Sir Charles came in. I guess Lee and Lester both went back to California, and I decided I was going to strike out on my own. So I formed the trio, and...
